item.title: China-Canada cooperation shows that diversification is about more paths forward
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 01:07:00
Diversification Illustration: Liu Xidan/GT Even as external speculation continues over whether Canada is "playing the China card," the tangible benefits of China-Canada cooperation are already becoming evident. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is currently in Shenzhen, China to attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Wednesday and Thursday. Ahead of the event, his remarks on the future of Canada's auto industry attracted considerable media attention. He said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with US fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Asked whether he was using potential Chinese investment as a leverage in negotiations with Washington, Carney replied: "It's not leverage. But action, reaction." Some foreign media outlets were quick to portray the move as Canada "playing the China card" in an attempt to pressure the US in the negotiations. Such interpretations take an unnecessarily narrow view of normal economic and trade cooperation and the expansion of diversified partnerships. Liu Dan, a research fellow at the Center for Regional and Country Studies at Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, told the Global Times on Tuesday that Carney's remarks reflect Canada's reassessment of the policy space for auto cooperation with China amid changing prospects for North American economic integration. Cooperation that was once considered a sensitive issue is increasingly becoming a practical policy option. This is both a pragmatic consideration as Canada diversifies its partnerships and a natural extension of the steady improvement in China-Canada economic relations since the beginning of this year, she added. Diversified partnerships are not bargaining chips to be brought out at the last minute, nor are they gestures designed to put pressure on any particular country. They are a practical response to an increasingly uncertain world. Canada is reassessing its economic partnerships and translating that shift into concrete diplomatic action. Carney's diplomatic itinerary this year shows Canada is working to build a broader network of partnerships. From seeking to become the first "associate member" of the European Union to pushing for trade negotiations with ASEAN and actively restoring and deepening economic and trade ties with China, Carney has effectively made the diversification of economic partnerships a central feature of his global agenda. With its vast market and comprehensive industrial system, China is an indispensable node in this network. China's enormous economic scale offers extensive opportunities for its trading partners. Every substantive dialogue can open up new markets, while every cooperation agreement has the potential to translate into orders, investment and tangible industrial development. During Carney's visit to China in January, the two sides reached specific agreements to address trade issues related to electric vehicles and agricultural products, and the resulting adjustments have already begun to pay dividends. According to Canadian media, Canadian exports to China surged by roughly 40 per cent in the first nine months of this year - an increase that far outpaces growth in exports to anywhere else. On the first day in Shenzhen, he also announced a series of new partnerships with China, covering trade and cultural measures including an expansion of current tariff agreements, more flights and agreements on education and the arts. Liu said China-Canada economic and trade cooperation remains centered on goods such as agricultural products, energy and consumer goods, but has considerable potential to expand beyond bilateral trade into industrial cooperation. China has well-established supply chains for batteries and auto components, while Canada has critical mineral resources and a strategic geographic position for exports. The two sides therefore have room to explore cooperation in joint auto manufacturing ventures, local supply chains and technology licensing. Since March, 16,211 Chinese electric vehicles have been imported into Canada. BYD has begun selling vehicles in Canada, while Geely announced in October that it expects to start selling electric vehicles in the Canadian market next year. These developments show that the growth of China-Canada economic and trade ties is neither a political show of diplomatic rhetoric nor a geopolitical arrangement directed against any third party. Improving bilateral relations have created market opportunities, policy adjustments have unlocked trade potential, and high-level dialogue has provided businesses with more expectations for cooperation. The potential expansion of trade benefits into industrial cooperation is therefore a natural next step in deepening bilateral economic ties. The world has changed, and countries cannot keep relying on old maps to find their way in a new economic landscape. China-Canada cooperation shows that geographical distance and differences in political systems should never make certain economic cooperation a "taboo." Diversification is not about proving to anyone that a country has an alternative way out; it is about giving itself more paths forward.

item.title: Looking out to the Pacific from Shenzhen Bay: Asia-Pacific co-op's roadmap becomes clearer: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 00:52:00
From left, Tian Wei, CGTN moderator, Robin Zeng, founder, chairman and CEO of CATL, Simon Trott, CEO of Rio Tinto, Robin Li, co-founder and CEO of Baidu, and Suzanne Clark, president and CEO of the US Chamber of Commerce, sit on the stage at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit held ahead of the APEC China 2026 summit in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, on November 17, 2026. Photo: VCG The 2026 APEC CEO Summit is held in Shenzhen from Tuesday to Wednesday. More than 2,000 representatives from political and business circles across 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies gathered in Qianhai, with 115 Fortune Global 500 companies in attendance. Among the participating economies, major US corporations including Boeing, HP, Citigroup, and Google accounted for the largest share - nearly 20 percent - taking part to discuss the next phase of business cooperation and development in the Asia-Pacific. At this historic moment, with the world's eyes fixed on Shenzhen, the summit, themed "To Prosper and Win the Future Together" - conveyed the global business community's confidence in the Asia-Pacific as the world's most dynamic economic region and a primary engine of global growth, as well as their expectations for China, in its capacity as host, to lead the way in fostering Asia-Pacific cooperation. A year ago, at the APEC CEO Summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, President Xi Jinping delivered a solemn message to the Asia-Pacific region and the world: "Walking with China means walking with opportunities, believing in China means believing in tomorrow, and investing in China means investing in the future." Over the past year, the Chinese economy has forged ahead despite mounting pressures, shifting toward new drivers of growth and higher-quality development, delivering a robust, substantive phased report for good start of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30). Amid the spillover effects of geopolitical conflicts and global industrial supply chains strained by energy crises and protectionism, China has not only demonstrated remarkable composure and resilience but has also - through high-standard opening-up - provided invaluable certainty to the Asia-Pacific and global economies. This powerfully validates the visionary insight that "the 'next China' is still China." At present, cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region faces new circumstances and new issues. The spread of anti-globalization sentiment, coupled with the rise of unilateralism and protectionism, is undermining the foundations of free and open trade and hindering the development of a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP). The international landscape is marked by turbulence and complexity; geopolitical rivalries are intensifying, and there is a growing tendency to politicize economic and trade issues or overstretch the security issue - all of which create divisions and obstacles for regional cooperation. Furthermore, significant development disparities among APEC members continue to constrain the overall effectiveness of regional cooperation. At this critical historical juncture, addressing the development challenges of the Asia-Pacific and unlocking the full potential of regional cooperation requires, more than ever, visionary guidance and concrete, actionable pathways. The times call for Chinese wisdom and Chinese solutions. Since the 2014 APEC meeting in Beijing, which prompted participating economies to endorse the roadmap for APEC's Contribution to the Realization of the FTAAP and the APEC Connectivity Blueprint for 2015-2025, China has consistently stood on the right side of history over the past decade. From advancing the FTAAP toward tangible progress to facilitating the implementation of the Connectivity Blueprint across land and sea, China has consistently stood on the right side of history, and created shared opportunities for the Asia-Pacific region through its own opening-up and development, while providing direction and momentum for regional cooperation through forward-looking ideas and pragmatic actions. At this critical historical juncture, China hoists the banner for advancing Asia-Pacific cooperation, which is not only of great significance in opening a new chapter in regional development, but will also inject more positive energy into global economic growth and international cooperation. As the host, China has fully leveraged the APEC CEO Summit as a bridge, consistently taking concrete steps to build consensus among regional businesses and remove obstacles to cooperation. The Shenzhen summit will launch a Shenzhen initiative at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit, marking the first time in the summit's 30-year history that an outcome document will be issued in the form of an initiative. The document will systematically incorporate and consolidate the business community's key proposals and offer recommendations to the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. The roadmap for Asia-Pacific cooperation is becoming clearer. During the summit, Chinese and international participants will engage in business dialogues under the theme "new landscape of the Asia-Pacific economy and opportunities for cooperation." The discussions will cover seven topics: connectivity, AI, sustainable development, the FTAAP, digital economy cooperation, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, and the coordinated digital and green transition. These topics not only reflect the forefront of global industrial transformation but also address the shared development aspirations of Asia-Pacific economies. They represent both a "wish list" and an "action list" for cooperation, offering targeted approaches to overcoming growth challenges and unlocking the potential for collaboration. Looking back at the history of Asia-Pacific cooperation, following the prevailing trends and seizing opportunities have been consistent themes. From Juncao and upland rice technology in the highlands of Papua New Guinea and Luban Workshops in Southeast Asian countries to the Punta Sierra Wind Farm in Chile and the Cirata Floating Solar Power Plant in Indonesia which Chinese companies helped build, China has consistently been willing to listen to the voices of developing and smaller economies within the Asia-Pacific family. It has also responded to the business community's shared aspirations to reduce trade barriers and facilitate the free flow of factors. By sharing opportunities through openness and pursuing win-win outcomes through cooperation, China has helped lay a solid foundation for the "Asia-Pacific miracle." Looking out toward the Pacific Ocean from Shenzhen Bay, one sees a region vast enough to accommodate the shared aspirations of all sides for prosperity. By translating their commitment to openness into mutually beneficial actions and pooling their innovative strengths to drive regional growth, the Asia-Pacific business community can surely write a new chapter in the "Asia-Pacific miracle," turn the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality, and inject sustained and powerful momentum into a world undergoing turbulence and transformation.

item.title: President Xi meets Asia-Pacific leaders ahead of APEC meeting；bilateral talks energize ties and lay groundwork for regional consensus: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 00:48:00
An APEC-themed installation is seen in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: Xinhua Ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting set to unfold Wednesday and Thursday in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, Chinese President Xi Jinping held a series of bilateral meetings on Tuesday with leaders from multiple Asia-Pacific economies. This intensive round of head-of-state diplomacy sets bilateral priorities before leaders gather for multilateral deliberations. Chinese experts said that such engagements embody a well-established practice in China's diplomacy of using multilateral occasions to advance bilateral relations, while translating bilateral consensus into building broader regional understanding. APEC provides a platform for both bilateral engagement and multilateral cooperation, creating opportunities for leaders to address differences and improve relations through direct exchanges, Chen Fengying, a research fellow at the Beijing-based China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, told the Global Times on Tuesday. At a time of complex international dynamics, high-level exchanges can chart directions for regional cooperation and help translate support for multilateralism into practical action, experts said. Head-of-state diplomacy sets direction Xi on Tuesday morning met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, according to the Xinhua News Agency. During their meeting, Xi said that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said, according to Xinhua. The meeting came as the two countries work to improve relations and expand cooperation. A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Tuesday afternoon that in addition to the two-year tariff exemption, under the supplementary arrangement, Canada will further expand exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminum products. Meanwhile, China will make additional adjustments to its anti-discrimination measures against certain Canadian agricultural and aquatic products in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The meeting with Carney was part of a packed day of bilateral diplomacy. Xi also met with Papua New Guinea (PNG) Prime Minister James Marape; General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam; Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo; Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori; and Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, Xinhua reported. Chinese experts believed that head-of-state diplomacy helps advance China's diplomatic outreach covering major countries, neighboring states and developing economies. These face-to-face, in-depth exchanges with leaders from diverse economies allow China to share its strategic assessments and cooperation propositions directly, manage differences, consolidate mutual trust, and lay solid groundwork for deliverables from the multilateral session, they argued. Wang Yiwei, professor at the School of International Studies, Renmin University of China, told the Global Times on Tuesday that the APEC event creates precious windows for high level interactions, facilitating visiting foreign leaders to take the opportunity for in person engagement with China's top leadership to inject fresh impetus into bilateral relations, and these conversations advance bilateral cooperation in parallel with wider regional agendas. Bilateral talks build broader consensus Experts said such head-of-state diplomacy steers Asia-Pacific cooperation with strategic vision. Upholding dialogue over confrontation and partnership rather than alliance, it encourages all parties to focus on shared development and jointly preserve the dynamism of the Asia-Pacific as the primary engine of global growth. It facilitates separate, candid exchanges with diverse Asia-Pacific partners, managing differences and identifying areas of alignment to pool gains from bilateral cooperation into collective momentum for joint Asia-Pacific action. The different priorities discussed on Tuesday showed how bilateral engagement can contribute to regional goals, from industrial development to environmental governance and multilateral coordination. In his meeting with Marape, Xi said the two sides should strengthen coordination within multilateral fora such as the United Nations and APEC, uphold international fairness and justice, expand cooperation in tackling climate change and protecting the marine environment, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xinhua reported. When meeting with To Lam, Xi said that in recent years, the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries have maintained close exchanges and reached important consensus on building a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance. This has helped advance bilateral relations and injected positive energy into regional peace and development, Xi added, according to Xinhua. APEC brings together economies with different sizes, needs and stages of development, Wang noted. Those differences provide concrete starting points for cooperation, Wang said. PNG's interest in agriculture, for example, creates opportunities for cooperation in agricultural digitalization and more convenient customs clearance and quarantine procedures. Vietnam's industrialization needs offer scope for closer industrial cooperation. During his meeting with Sheinbaum, Xi said that advancing China-Mexico relations to new heights, across broader areas and in greater depth is of great significance to implementing their respective national development strategies and supporting the Global South in seeking strength through unity, according to Xinhua. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. When talking with Kast in Shenzhen, Xi noted that the most valuable experience guiding bilateral ties is mutual respect, equality and win-win results. During his meeting with Fujimori, Xi noted that the protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement took effect officially about two weeks ago, and the Chancay Port, built with the participation of Chinese enterprises, has given a strong boost to economic and trade cooperation between Asia and Latin America. Wang said the emphasis on different partners' concerns reflects an effort to find common ground and build consensus while accommodating differences. China can also work with partners on traditional and new infrastructure, the digital transformation of industry, the development of digital industries and green energy, Wang said. Responding to these needs helps give substance to a shared regional agenda. The constructive tone of these meetings was also reflected in international media reporting. Reuters reported on Tuesday that Carney pointed to "greater predictability and stability" in China-Canada relations, with the Associated Press also reporting that Carney saw the stabilizing bilateral trade as indicative of how the two countries could work together pragmatically to solve problems. Vietnamese broadcaster Voice of Vietnam on Tuesday reported about the bilateral meeting between Chinese and Vietnamese leaders, pointing to bilateral political trust, trade, investment and strategic infrastructure connectivity. It also highlighted To Lam's hope that Vietnam could build on the outcomes of China's APEC host year as it prepares to host the forum in 2027. Chen said that bilateral meetings at the leadership level can lay a solid foundation for a successful APEC gathering. Exchanges before the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting help foster a positive atmosphere, coordinate positions and build consensus, Chen said. Signals emerging from these one-on-one conversations carry weight for the subsequent multilateral deliberations.

item.title: GT Voice: When K-pop meets robotics: new potential for China-SK tech co-op
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 23:56:00
Visitors watch an intelligent robot dance performance at an aquarium in Qinhuangdao, North China's Hebei Province, on October 7, 2026. Many parents and children visited the aquarium on the last day of the seven-day National Day holidays. Photo: IC When humanoid robots took to the runway and danced to K-pop music in Hong Kong on Monday, the performance offered more than a glimpse of futuristic entertainment. It illustrated how Chinese robotics technology and South Korean entertainment content can be brought together to explore new commercial opportunities. Chinese firm Star Plus Legend Holdings and South Korea's Galaxy Corp signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on Monday to expand their existing cooperation into robot entertainment and artificial intelligence (AI) robotics. According to an announcement, the planned collaboration covers robot parks, global robot tours and the joint development of AI toys and companion robots targeting markets in China, South Korea and beyond. The partnership provides a fresh perspective on the potential of China-South Korea economic cooperation, with companies from the two countries bringing their complementary strengths and joining hands in exploring new business opportunities. Chinese robotics company Unitree participated in the performance, while Galaxy Corp brought its experience in entertainment content and robot performances. Star Plus Legend has established cooperation with Unitree to develop consumer robots incorporating entertainment intellectual property (IP). What makes this cooperation particularly noteworthy is that it goes beyond a single performance or business agreement. The two companies established a partnership in November 2025, when Star Plus Legend acquired a stake of no more than 7 percent in Galaxy through an investment fund. Their initial cooperation covered concerts, exhibitions and entertainment IP development. The latest MOU extends that relationship into the joint development of robotics products and entertainment applications. The partnership also points to a broader opportunity for China-South Korea economic cooperation. While the two countries have long been connected through trade and industrial supply chains, the latest collaboration shows how businesses can go a step further by combining their strengths to jointly develop new products and consumer experiences. In emerging industries such as embodied AI, this cooperation could help turn technological capabilities into commercial opportunities and create new sources of demand. For robotics companies, one of the key challenges is finding applications that can translate technological advances into sustainable commercial demand. Entertainment offers a possible testing ground. Robot performances, interactive venues and consumer products based on popular characters could help companies explore how embodied AI might reach a broader consumer market. Some initial applications are already taking shape. According to Star Plus Legend's announcement, Galaxy operates the Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul, where visitors can experience robot performances and interactions. These examples suggest that the integration of entertainment IP and robotics is beginning to move beyond demonstrations into physical commercial spaces, although its longer-term business potential remains to be tested. The potential value of such cooperation is not limited to the Chinese and South Korean markets. Galaxy founder and chief executive Choi Yong-ho expressed hope that businesses from the two countries could work together to explore international opportunities, according to local Hong Kong media. The latest business partnership also comes against the backdrop of growing exchanges between China and South Korea in emerging technologies. On November 3, a forum on embodied AI technology and industrial cooperation was held in Seoul, bringing together representatives from government institutions, research organizations, universities and enterprises from both countries. Discussions focused on core technologies, industrial applications, commercialization challenges and technical standards. The forum followed a China-South Korea science and technology innovation exchange conference held in Seoul on October 28, which focused on AI, embodied intelligence and advanced manufacturing. Taken together, these exchanges indicate that the two countries are exploring cooperation in a range of emerging industries. Against this backdrop, the significance of the Hong Kong partnership goes beyond robots dancing to K-pop. It illustrates a new positive trend for China-South Korea economic cooperation in which manufacturing capabilities, emerging technologies and creative content are brought together to develop new products and markets. If such cooperation can move from individual projects to sustainable commercial applications, it could create fresh opportunities for businesses on both sides and inject new momentum into bilateral economic ties.

item.title: APEC CEO Summit shows why dialogue still beats barriers
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 23:07:00
APEC China 2026. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT Walking down the streets of Shenzhen, lines of banners champion "Openness, Innovation, Cooperation" adorn the palm-lined boulevards. As the Chinese coastal metropolis has fully entered "APEC time," more than 2,000 political and business leaders from the 21 APEC economies, as well as 13 non-member economies including the UK, France and Germany, gathered in the city on Tuesday for the 2026 APEC CEO Summit. The summit builds on the deliberations of the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) - APEC's official private-sector advisory body. It serves as a high-level forum where business leaders, from APEC's member economies of all sizes as well as non-member economies, can bring market perspectives to top policymakers. Experts said the platform gives the Asia-Pacific business community a collective voice, proving that dialogue beats barriers at a time when economic fragmentation threatens such voices from being heard. Several foreign guests attending the 2026 APEC CEO Summit expressed a shared view during interviews with the Global Times that amid rising protectionism and growing policy uncertainty, businesses need predictable rules and a fair cooperative environment, not tariffs and barriers. They regard China as a stabilizing force in the regional economy and a reliable partner, believing that the country plays a key role in advancing Asia-Pacific cooperation and balancing the global order. Voices for cooperation As the highest-level business dialogue platform under APEC, the 2026 APEC CEO Summit brought together not only leaders of Asia-Pacific economies, government officials and heads of international organizations, but also a large number of executives from Fortune Global 500 companies and leading tech innovators, with US companies accounting for more than 20 percent of participating businesses. "This year, as in previous years, the largest contingent - the largest number of CEOs and companies - comes from the US," Sean Stein, President of the US-China Business Council, told the Global Times on Tuesday. According to Stein, APEC is perhaps the only international body designed from the very beginning to give businesses the microphone. Discussions unfolding over the two-day CEO Summit will bring together business recommendations for dialogue with the political side, he said. "That's the magic of APEC. It's when you bring business and governments together to solve problems and forge solutions," he noted. According to an official program, executives from Chinese and foreign enterprises attended the summit. The lineup spans industries from batteries and robotics to aviation, logistics and payments, with executives participating in discussions on regional trade, connectivity and the digital economy. Wang Xingxing, chairman of Unitree Robotics, emphasized during the discussions the importance of focusing on the future development scale of the robotics industry and called for cooperation as the only way to make the industry's pie bigger. Wang Chuanfu, chairman and president of BYD Group, said that a "win-lose" approach cannot last, and that the company is promoting the global spread of Chinese technology through local procurement and research and development. On the sidelines of the summit, several interviewed foreign attendees expressed optimism about the prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation and affirmed China's positive role in promoting regional cooperation and safeguarding an open economy. "To move goods efficiently reduces costs for businesses and lowers production costs. There are so many unnecessary restrictions, and those trade restrictions are creating problems," Carlos Kuriyama, director of the APEC Policy Support Unit at the APEC Secretariat, told the Global Times on Tuesday. "And that's why APEC is very important, because we have 21 members, some of whom are the largest economies in the world, gathering here to discuss all these challenges, share their problems, and find ways together to [develop] solutions," he said. The APEC business community can prosper by balancing competition with cooperation, especially as businesses seek more efficient and resilient supply chains in an ever-changing global environment, Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat, told the Global Times on Tuesday. Pedrosa noted that a more stable global economy could emerge. With the WTO, APEC and regional trade organizations now in place, he said that there must be space for new rules to develop amid rapid tech innovations, and that "China can help open that conversation." Zhou Mi, a senior research fellow at the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation, told the Global Times that the exchange of views between Chinese and foreign business communities at the summit reflects their shared concerns about current development priorities. "It helps leaders of various economies clearly understand what businesses support, hope for and need. This is a key mechanism for businesses to play an important role. APEC itself advocates freedom and openness, aiming to provide more sustained momentum for all parties by stimulating the vitality of enterprises and the market," Zhou said. Seeking for opportunities Interviews with Chinese and foreign business leaders, as well as delegations from South Korea, the UK, Australia and Malaysia, revealed packed schedules in Shenzhen and one clear commonality: They arrived with urgent, practical industrial needs, seeking solutions and partners. A representative from the UK tech delegation said their purpose was to deepen AI cooperation with Chinese companies. Developing economies at a critical stage of green transition and industrial upgrading went directly to BYD and Nanshan district's automated workshops and lithium-battery firms to explore what Shenzhen's new energy and solar industries can offer. Ben Faes, group chief executive officer of RWS in the UK, highlighted the openness and collaboration he experienced in Shenzhen. "Everything I've seen so far, all the welcomes, really encourages me to do more business in the region," he told the Global Times. "APEC [region] is the fastest growing region for my company. I guess one keyword would be hope," Faes noted. According to data from China's Ministry of Commerce, total regional trade of APEC members grew from $3.1 trillion in 1989 to about $26 trillion in 2025, providing important support for global economic growth. China is continuously strengthening its growth momentum, market opportunities, supply support and stable expectations. "China is a formidable engine for the development of the world, not only in terms of the ability to produce things that are necessary for our lives, but also to innovate and bring balance to the world order, which is very necessary," Faes noted.

item.title: Taiwan island does not operate in Papua New Guinea anymore, PNG PM says in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 22:34:00
View of Port Moresby, the capital city of Papua New Guinea File photo: VCG Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape said on Tuesday that the island of Taiwan does not operate in the country anymore, during a meeting with Chinese leader in Shenzhen ahead of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, according to The Guardian. "China respects the sovereignty of Papua New Guinea. We must give full respect for the sovereignty of China," Marape was quoted as saying in a Reuters report. Taiwan regional authorities claimed in early November that it had decided to shut "Taipei Economic Office" in Papua New Guinea and stop buying liquefied natural gas from the country, Reuters reported. When addressing a related question, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on November 9 that the decision by the government of Papua New Guinea to close the "Taipei Economic Office" in Papua New Guinea once again shows that upholding the one-China principle is where international public opinion trends and the arc of history bends. China appreciates this and will continue working with Papua New Guinea to firmly support each other's core interests and major concerns. China stands ready to increase imports of liquefied natural gas from Papua New Guinea, deepen cooperation in economy and trade and other areas, and add new dimensions to our comprehensive strategic partnership. Global Times

item.title: Diving 4,600 meters into the Pacific aboard Jiaolong: An underwater climb reveals the wonder, skill and patience behind deep-sea exploration
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 22:17:00
Inside a titanium sphere just over two meters across, Global Times reporter watched the Pacific disappear into darkness. The depth reading kept climbing, the cabin grew colder and a question began to intrude on the excitement: What had led to this moment? The answer began on October 26, when the Global Times reporter joined the research vessel Deep Sea No. 1 and its manned submersible Jiaolong for a monthlong scientific expedition. On November 2, that journey took the reporter to the seabed some 4,600 meters below the surface, in the Ontong Java Plateau region of the South Pacific. For someone who grew up following science news and stories of exploration, the chance to descend in Jiaolong felt like a childhood dream come true. Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea had given generations of readers a way to imagine such a journey. Now, the reporter was about to embark on the said journey, with a pilot and an engineer in place of Captain Nemo. Jiaolong had long been a familiar name in the news. China's first independently designed and integrated deep-sea manned submersible reached 7,062 meters in 2012, a milestone in the country's exploration of the ocean. At about 8.7 meters long and 4 meters wide, it carries cameras, robotic arms and thrusters around a pressure-resistant cabin built to hold three people. Crew members aboard the Shenhai-1 support vessel detach the main lifting cable from the Jiaolong manned submersible in preparation for its dive on November 1, 2026. Its hundreds of dives offered reassurance, but the prospect of becoming one of its occupants brought a nervousness familiar to anyone boarding an aircraft for the first time. Two days before the dive, pilot Fu Wentao took the reporter through the safeguards. Jiaolong was designed to operate at depths of 7,000 meters, well beyond this mission's destination. Its ballast weights, he explained, were held by electromagnets and designed to drop away if power failed, allowing the submersible to become buoyant and rise. Backup systems provided further protection, while a typical dive used no more than about half the main battery's charge. Understanding these arrangements helped settle everyone's nerves. Fu also outlined the mission: descend to around 4,600 meters, travel roughly 2 kilometers along the seabed, then begin the ascent from higher ground. The entire dive would last about 10 hours. Food, extra clothing and heat packs were prepared alongside the scientific equipment. Into the darkness Early that morning, after equipment checks, pilot Tang Jialing, engineer Wang Xiangxin and the reporter climbed into Jiaolong. The spherical cabin was compact, with instruments taking up much of the space around the crew, but each person had a porthole through which to watch the world outside. Beside the two smaller side windows were hand controls for the external cameras. Above Tang's central position, a panel held switches for communications, equipment power and ballast release. In front of him were controls for maneuvering the submersible and operating its hydraulic robotic arms, which would become the crew's hands on the seabed. Crew members aboard the Shenhai-1 support vessel detach the main lifting cable from the Jiaolong manned submersible in preparation for its dive on November 1, 2026. Deep Sea No. 1 's lifting system lowered the crew into the water, where divers detached the securing lines. Jiaolong then took in seawater through its ballast system and began to sink, drifting down like a falling leaf. At roughly 40 meters a minute, the descent would take about two hours, leaving time to eat and review the work ahead. What struck the reporter first was the stillness. The sea surface could be restless and changeable; beyond the windows, the water seemed motionless. Increasing pressure announced itself only through the instruments. There was no view into the distance, just darkness and the knowledge that more water was gathering overhead. For years, the reporter had followed Jiaolong through reports of depth records and the samples it brought back. Inside the cabin, those achievements revealed themselves with more human scales: a pilot checking his instruments, an engineer preparing for the work below, and a team aboard the mother ship monitoring the dive. The cabin was not silent. An acoustic communications system developed by the Chinese Academy of Sciences kept the crew in contact with Deep Sea No. 1 , transmitting updates on the position, depth and condition. Its pulses reminded the reporter of dolphin calls. Pilot Tang Jialing checks the status of China's manned submersible Jiaolong during a dive on November 2, 2026. Photos on this page: Feng Fan/Global Times Once the depth display passed 4,000 meters, Tang began preparing for the arrival. He checked the submersible's condition and attitude, switched on the external lights and watched for the bottom. As the submersible approached the seabed, he released the descent ballast, bringing the long downward journey to an end. The view changed abruptly. Rocks and patches of sediment emerged in the lights, recorded by Jiaolong 's 4K cameras. After the darkness of the descent, the brightly lit foreground looked almost familiar, its pale green cast reminding the reporter of shallower water seen while snorkeling. Moving through it required equipment built for a very different environment. Chinese-made thrusters, powered by domestic lithium battery packs, drove the more than 20-ton submersible forward. Researchers aboard Deep Sea No. 1 had explained that overseas technology restrictions had encouraged the replacement of imported components, while improvements among Chinese suppliers increasingly offered better alternatives. Here, those changes were carrying the crew across the seabed. Climbing underwater mountain The assignment was to collect deep-water and geological samples and examine the terrain along the route. Deep Sea No. 1 had already mapped the area from the surface, but the map could not show every detail the crew now encountered through the windows. Tang watched the ground ahead, looking for changes in the rocks and places worth sampling. A display tracked the route against the planned course and showed the mother ship's position overhead. Jiaolong 's 475th dive soon produced a useful observation: a patch of seabed dotted with nodules, whose location the team surveyed and recorded before continuing toward higher ground. Animal sightings were scattered. Grenadier fish and squat lobsters appeared along the way, while sponges nestled in crevices like small white roses. The longer the reporter watched, the more the reporter understood how easily an unfamiliar form of life could be overlooked among the rocks. A screen inside Jiaolong displays its robotic arm working on the seafloor on November 2, 2026. Close inspection of such habitats has already brought discoveries. During Jiaolong expeditions in 2023 and 2024, scientists found a previously unknown worm living inside glass sponges on northwestern Pacific seamounts at around 1,000 meters deep, according to the Second Institute of Oceanography under China's Ministry of Natural Resources. Named Eunice siphoninsidiator, the worm shelters in the sponge's central cavity and ambushes other small animals living there. Its Chinese name evokes an assassin. What looks like a quiet sponge can conceal a relationship between species that scientists are only now beginning to understand. After about two hours of exploration along the bottom, the team reached the foot of a rocky underwater mountain. Examining the rocks, Wang tentatively identified basalt, suggesting that the formation had been built by volcanic activity. Dark, tightly packed rock covered its slopes. As Jiaolong climbed, the scenery grew stranger. Shrimp drifted past like slivers of ice. Farther up, sponges rose on slender stalks that appeared to stretch 3 or 4 meters, their broad tops opening into the water like butterfly nets left suspended in the deep. The difficulty became clear when he tried to retrieve a rock from the mountainside. Each pause near the bottom could disturb sediment, sending a cloud across the view. Waiting for it to clear meant holding position on a slope; moving without a clear view risked bringing the submersible too close to the rock face. Tang was one of China's first Jiaolong pilots. After more than 18 years working with the vehicle and helping to upgrade its equipment, he knew its movements intimately. Yet even that experience could not make every attempt straightforward. He found a promising rock and steadied Jiaolong . Looking between the porthole and the camera display, he extended the robotic arm and closed the gripper around it. The rock lifted from the seabed, but before it reached the sample basket, it slipped free and fell. Disturbed sediment spread across the window like a sandstorm. For a while, the rock disappeared. The team had to wait for the water to clear enough to try again, conscious that the specimen might slide farther down the slope. As visibility began to return, Tang leaned forward from his kneeling position at the controls, bringing his face close to the window. The cabin wall was cold, but his attention remained fixed outside. Both hands worked the controls as he searched for the fallen rock, aligned the arm and adjusted the gripper. This time, the rock held. Slowly, he drew it toward Jiaolong and lowered it into the sample basket. The reporter had imagined deep-sea exploration in terms of extraordinary depths and unfamiliar creatures. Watching that rock finally come aboard, the reporter began to appreciate how much of it consisted of patient, exacting work. The specimen would reach researchers on the surface because someone had persisted with it here. On that submerged mountain, the Global Times reporter thought of the answer famously attributed to British mountaineer George Mallory when asked why he wanted to climb Everest: "Because it's there." The same curiosity had brought the team down through 4,600 meters of water, though curiosity alone could not put a rock in the basket. That took Tang's hands, Jiaolong 's engineering and the people waiting above on Deep Sea No. 1 . Beyond the reach of the lights, the mountain continued. The crew had collected a small piece of it; there was still far more to see.

item.title: China-Laos Railway cross-border passenger trips top 300,000 for first time in 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 21:18:00
A train crosses a viaduct on the China-Laos Railway Photo: Courtesy of China Railway Kunming Group Co. The China-Laos Railway has handled more than 300,000 cross-border passenger trips so far this year, surpassing the annual threshold for the first time since international passenger services began in 2023, as the railway increasingly serves as a vital link for tourism, people-to-people exchanges and regional economic cooperation. The railway had recorded 300,600 cross-border passenger trips as of November 16, according to data from China Railway Kunming Group Co. The milestone came after passenger traffic this year exceeded the full-year total for 2025 as early as October 21, underscoring growing demand for cross-border travel, China Railway Kunming Group Co told the Global Times in a statement on Tuesday. Chinese experts said the sustained growth in passenger traffic reflects improvements in transport capacity and cross-border services, while creating new opportunities for tourism investment, industrial cooperation and broader regional integration. Since international passenger services were launched on April 13, 2023, the number of daily passenger trains between Kunming, capital of Southwest China's Yunnan Province, and Vientiane, the Lao capital, has increased from two to four. Cross-border seating capacity per train has expanded from 250 to 420, while customs clearance time at Mohan railway port has been shortened to about 50 minutes, according to railway authorities. The improvements have made same-day travel between Kunming and Vientiane increasingly convenient, while expanded multilingual services, dedicated international ticket counters and support for overseas bank cards have made cross-border journeys easier for international travelers. These improvements have helped attract a more diverse range of international travelers. According to railway authorities, international passenger trains have accommodated a cumulative 978,000 cross-border passenger trips involving travelers from more than 120 countries and regions, while tourism-related consumption at scenic attractions, hotels and restaurants along the route has grown by more than 35 percent. Bian Yongzu, executive deputy editor-in-chief of Modernization of Management magazine, told the Global Times on Tuesday that transforming passenger traffic into tangible regional economic benefits is a gradual process that extends well beyond improving transportation. "In its initial stage, the railway mainly facilitated travel for local residents and attracted tourists. As passenger flows have increased, improvements in railway operations and services helped unlock broader economic opportunities," Bian said. Growing passenger traffic has encouraged more businesses and investors to explore opportunities along the railway, particularly in tourism, hospitality and related services, gradually translating improved connectivity into economic gains for communities along the route, he noted. Bian said the railway's growing economic impact could also encourage deeper cooperation between China and Laos in financing, investment, policy coordination and industrial development. As Laos becomes more closely integrated into regional industrial and supply chains, the railway could generate a wider demonstration effect, encouraging neighboring countries, including Thailand, to strengthen their transport connections with the railway network, he said. "This could create a snowball effect, attracting more investment and economic activity while expanding the railway's regional reach," Bian said, adding that Laos has the potential to develop into an important regional transport hub and a driver of economic growth. Beyond its economic significance, the railway has played an important role in strengthening people-to-people ties. China's large outbound tourism market has brought new opportunities to Laos, with growing numbers of Chinese travelers and tourism-related businesses contributing to the development of the local services industry, Bian said. The railway's growing passenger traffic comes alongside an expansion in freight transportation, highlighting its increasingly important role in regional connectivity, he added. Since opening on December 3, 2021, the railway has transported more than 90 million tons of cargo, including over 21 million tons of cross-border freight, according to official data released in August. In the first half of 2026, the value of imports and exports transported via the railway reached 17.17 billion yuan ($2.53 billion), up 33.8 percent year-on-year, the Xinhua News Agency reported. Official data released in October also showed that the cumulative value of foreign trade handled via the railway had exceeded 100 billion yuan, demonstrating its growing importance as a trade corridor linking China with Southeast Asia.

item.title: Chinese Embassy in Japan warns against off-season Mt Fuji climbing after tourist goes missing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 19:37:00
An aerial view of the snow-covered summit of Mount Fuji, seen from Tsuru, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan, on October 30, 2026. Photo: VCG The Chinese Embassy in Japan on Tuesday urged Chinese nationals not to climb mountains during closure periods, after a Chinese tourist went missing while attempting to climb Mount Fuji in violation of restrictions. The embassy said it had immediately contacted Japanese police, repeatedly urged them to organize search and rescue operations as soon as possible, and provided necessary assistance to the missing tourist's family, according to a release from the embassy. In the notice, the embassy warned that mountains in Japan, including Mount Fuji, frequently experience strong winds and blizzards during closure periods, while mountain rest facilities and first-aid centers suspend operations. It called on Chinese nationals in Japan to raise their safety awareness when engaging in outdoor activities and not to attempt to climb mountains during closure periods, in order to avoid danger. According to Japan's Mainichi Shimbun on November 13, the missing Chinese tourist was a man in his 20s. He began climbing Mount Fuji alone via the Yoshida Trail at Mount Fuji's fifth station in Yamanashi Prefecture on the morning of November 8. The man had initially planned to climb with two friends, but they abandoned the plan after learning that the mountain was closed for the season. The man continued climbing alone, local police said. According to a report by Japan's ABEMA TIMES on Tuesday, Japanese police continued their search for the missing Chinese tourist, but had yet to locate him as of Tuesday, nine days after he went missing. The man was not equipped with winter mountaineering gear such as crampons or ice axes, Mainichi Shimbun's report said. According to the official Mount Fuji climbing website, the climbing season for the Yoshida Trail normally runs from July 1 to September 10, and all routes leading to the summit are closed outside the designated climbing season. The website also warns that Mount Fuji becomes extremely dangerous outside the climbing season because of freezing temperatures, strong winds and unmaintained trails. Mountain huts and first-aid facilities are closed, leaving climbers without reliable shelter or emergency assistance. Global Times

item.title: Macao targets growth, economic diversification in 2027
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17 12:51:00
Chief Executive of the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) Sam Hou Fai delivers his annual policy address to the Legislative Assembly in Macao, south China, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka) China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) will seek to maintain economic growth in 2027 and accelerate economic diversification amid downward pressure, Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai said Monday. Delivering his annual policy address to the Legislative Assembly, Sam outlined plans to attract investment, develop financial services and expand international tourism while maintaining support for residents. The report identified rising social welfare spending and an excessive reliance on a single sector for fiscal revenue as an unsustainable combination. Macao's economy grew 2.9 percent year on year in real terms in the first three quarters of 2026, according to preliminary figures cited in the report. To support diversification, the government plans to launch an investment guidance fund, appoint professional fund managers and invest in projects that serve Macao's long-term development. It will seek to attract more projects to Macao and the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin. Financial sector measures include advancing securities legislation, attracting more domestic and overseas companies to issue bonds in Macao, and developing links between the digital pataca and the digital yuan. In tourism, the government will target markets including Europe, India and the Middle East, offering incentives for flights, hotels and cross-border transport to attract international visitors on multi-destination trips. The government will also continue its cash-sharing scheme, tax relief and household utility subsidies, and expand free childcare services and support for families. Chief Executive of the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) Sam Hou Fai delivers his annual policy address to the Legislative Assembly in Macao, south China, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka)
